Commands are grouped by level. `task` commands act on one task run, one
Planner–Builder–Reviewer execution of a task file. `roadmap` commands act on a roadmap.
Project commands stay at the top level.

```text
forgecycle task run <task.md> [--policy NAME] [--base REF] [--approval POLICY] [--planner ID] [--builder ID] [--reviewer ID] [--auto-resume]
forgecycle task status <task-run-id> [--json]
forgecycle task resume <task-run-id> [--feedback FILE] [--planner ID] [--builder ID] [--reviewer ID] [--auto-resume]
forgecycle task approve <task-run-id>
forgecycle task reject <task-run-id> <feedback.md>
forgecycle task abandon <task-run-id>
forgecycle task clean <task-run-id>

forgecycle roadmap decompose <plan.md> [--policy NAME] [--decomposer ID] [--output DIR]
forgecycle roadmap questions <DIR|roadmap.json> [--policy NAME] [--decomposer ID]
forgecycle roadmap run <DIR|roadmap.json> [--policy NAME] [--base REF] [--approval POLICY] [--planner ID] [--builder ID] [--reviewer ID] [--skip ID[,ID...]] [--auto-resume] [--accept-defaults]
forgecycle roadmap status <roadmap-run-id> [--json]
forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id> [--planner ID] [--builder ID] [--reviewer ID] [--auto-resume]
forgecycle roadmap abandon <roadmap-run-id>

forgecycle status [--json]
forgecycle pause
forgecycle unpause [--planner ID] [--builder ID] [--reviewer ID] [--auto-resume]
forgecycle init [config|skill] [--check|--force]
forgecycle doctor [--ping] [--ping-timeout SECONDS]
forgecycle prune [--worktrees] [--runs] [--force]
forgecycle serve [--port N] [--listen ADDR] [--public-url URL] [--no-auth] [--open]
forgecycle observe --summary [--workflow ID] [--json]
forgecycle update [vX.Y.Z] [--check] [--force]
forgecycle version
forgecycle help [task|roadmap] [command]
```

Running `forgecycle` with no arguments prints the same help as `forgecycle help`.
`-h` or `--help` anywhere among a command's arguments prints that command's help:
its usage, arguments, options with their defaults, and notes, wrapped to 79
columns. The overview also lists every exit status.

Options follow the usual Unix conventions. They may come before or after
the arguments; a value may follow the option (`--policy economy`) or an `=`
(`--policy=economy`); `--` ends the options; and when an option is repeated,
the last value wins. A usage error exits 64 and prints the command and a
pointer to its help on stderr:

```text
forgecycle: error: task run: unknown option '--bogus'
Try 'forgecycle task run --help'.
```

One task can have several task runs (a retry after an abandon, or a rerun on
another base), and one roadmap can have several roadmap runs, so commands
take the run ID that `task run` or `roadmap run` prints, never a task file or
a roadmap task ID such as `FC02` (except in `--skip`).

Approval policies are `autonomous`, `plan-and-final`, `every-turn`, and `custom`.
When stdin and stdout are terminals, approval gates offer an inline confirmation;
detached and CI runs stop with exit 21 for `task approve` or `task reject` to handle later.
Routing policies are project-defined and normally named `economy`, `balanced`,
and `quality`. Each policy must define four ordered candidate lists, one per
role: `decomposer`, `planner`, `builder`, and `reviewer`; `forgecycle doctor` verifies them, and
`forgecycle doctor --ping` also sends each candidate they use a one-line, billed
read-only prompt to prove its credentials, model, and effort work.

To switch agents without editing configuration, name the role:
`--planner ID`, `--builder ID`, or `--reviewer ID` replaces that role's list
with one configured candidate, for that invocation only. `task run`,
`task resume`, `roadmap run`, and `roadmap resume` accept all three; a
read-only candidate cannot be `--builder`. `--decomposer ID` does the same
for `roadmap decompose` and `roadmap questions`.
After a stop, the `forgecycle: next:` lines name the flag of the role that
acts next.

```bash
# use the "economy" policy's candidates for this task run
forgecycle task run tasks/task-003.md --policy economy

# builder-agy ran out of tokens; build with builder-claude for this invocation
forgecycle task resume 20260918T101500Z-add-the-store-abc123 --builder builder-claude

# a blocked review: retry it, and any later review, with claude-high
forgecycle task resume 20260918T101500Z-add-the-store-abc123 --reviewer claude-high
```

`task resume` prints the phase it re-enters and the role that will read your
feedback, for example `resuming into building (turn 4); feedback
003-human-feedback.md will be read by Builder`.

When a task run stops, it prints why and what to do next. `forgecycle task status
<task-run-id>` shows the same report later. Each stop records a stable `stop_kind`
in `state.json`, such as `agent_failure`, `needs_human`, or `approval_gate`.
Steps marked `(human decision)` need a person; the others are safe for an
operating agent to take.

```text
forgecycle: info: Run blocked: all candidates failed: builder-agy: quota_exhausted (...)
forgecycle: stop: status=blocked kind=agent_failure detail=quota_exhausted exit=20
forgecycle: stop: resumes into building (turn 4); feedback is read by Builder
forgecycle: stop: inspect .forgecycle/task-runs/<task-run-id>/003-reviewer-review.md
forgecycle: stop: inspect .forgecycle/task-runs/<task-run-id>/events.log
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume <task-run-id> --builder <candidate-id>  # continue building with a candidate that is not on a quota cooldown (forgecycle doctor lists them)
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>  # after the provider quota resets
```

See [Recovery](/documentation/guides/recovery/#reading-a-stop) for every stop kind.

With `--auto-resume`, `task run` and `task resume` resume a stopped task run
by themselves when the recovery is a plain `task resume` with no input (for
example an `unaccepted_head`, a `review_invariant`, or a timed-out
candidate), at most once between two accepted handoffs. Stops that need input,
a decision, or a wait, such as quota resets, still stop. The flag is off by
default because every automatic resume is a billed model call. See
[Automatic resume](/documentation/guides/recovery/#automatic-resume).

`forgecycle status` is the project overview. It shows which task run reserves
the repository and lists every task run and roadmap run that is not done or
abandoned, with its state, stop kind, and first next command, so the IDs are
easy to find after a crash or a killed terminal:

```text
Reservation: task run 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4
Task runs:
  20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4  blocked  agent_failure (quota_exhausted)  roadmap run 20261025T120000Z-orders-api-1f2e, FC02 attempt 2
    Next: forgecycle task resume 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4 --builder <candidate-id>
Roadmap runs:
  20261025T120000Z-orders-api-1f2e  stopped  task_run_stopped (agent_failure)  FC02 (2/3)
    Next: forgecycle roadmap resume 20261025T120000Z-orders-api-1f2e  # after task run 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4 is done or abandoned; an abandoned task restarts with a new task run
```

A stopped or interrupted task run keeps the reservation, so a second
`task run` is refused with exit 21. The refusal says how to free the
repository: the next steps for the task run that holds it, then
`task abandon` to discard that task run instead:

```text
forgecycle: error: Repository is reserved by run 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4
forgecycle: stop: reserved_by=20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4 status=building kind=interrupted
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4  # continue the interrupted run; it re-enters reviewing
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4 --reviewer <candidate-id>  # continue reviewing with another configured candidate, for example when a slow one was killed
forgecycle: next (human decision): forgecycle task abandon 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4  # discard it, keeping its branch and artifacts, and free the repository for another task run
```

Ctrl-C (or SIGTERM) stops a run cleanly: the running agent CLI is asked to
stop, a running gate's processes are stopped and its `cleanup` runs, and the
stop block names the command that continues the run. `--auto-resume` never
resumes after it. Press Ctrl-C again to exit at once. See
[Stop a run with Ctrl-C](/documentation/guides/recovery/#stop-a-run-with-ctrl-c).

To stop without losing the turn in progress, run `forgecycle pause` from
another terminal in the repository. It needs no ID: whatever runs there, a
task run or a roadmap run, stops once its current Planner, Builder, or
Reviewer turn ends, with the stop kind `pause_requested` and exit 21.
`forgecycle unpause` cancels a pause that has not taken effect yet, or
continues the paused run. See
[Pause after the current turn](/documentation/guides/recovery/#pause-after-the-current-turn).

Optional configuration covers worktree bootstrap (`worktree.copy_ignored`
copies Git-ignored local files such as `local.properties` into each worktree),
project command lint rules (`lint.command_rules`), review evidence reuse for
documentation-only changes (`review.evidence_reuse_paths`), gates that
ForgeCycle runs itself before each review for suites too long for an agent's
tool timeouts (`review.gates`; a plan marks a check of a gate's output
`after_gate`, and Reviewer runs it after the gates), quota cooldowns
(`quota_cooldown_seconds`), and a decomposition size budget
(`decompose.max_acceptance_criteria`). See [Configuration](/documentation/guides/configuration/).

Stable exit codes are `0` for done/success, `20` for blocked, `21` for a waiting
or paused run, `22` for failed, `64` for usage errors, `65` for invalid setup,
and `66` for direct protocol-validation failures.
